name: Mouha ou Hammou Zayani
aliasesRaw: Tamazight: Muḥa u Ḥemmu Aẓayyi · Moha ou Hammou · Mouha ou Hammou Zaïani / Zaïani / Zayani · Moha ou Hammou Azayi · Fr. archives: 'Moha ou Hammou', 'le caïd Hammou', 'Hammou des Zaïanes', 'le chef zaïan' · Sp.: Mohamed Hammou, 'el caíd Hammu', 'los zayanes' · Ar.: محا أو حمو الزياني

aliases.value: Mouha ou Hammou Zaïani / Zaïani / Zayani
aliases.folded: mouha ou hammou zaiani / zaiani / zayani

born: c. 1857 or c. 1863, Middle Atlas — not established
died: 27 March 1921 (some accounts spring 1921 without exact date), Azlag n'Tazemmourt / Azelag N'Tazemourte, Middle Atlas
oneLine: Qaid of the Zaian confederation, appointed by the Makhzen in the 1870s–80s; led the Zaian war against France 1914–1921 and commanded at El Herri.
contestedPoints: Year of his qaid appointment (1877 / 1880 / 1886). Birth year. Whether his son Hassan personally killed him or whether he died in a fight against a faction his sons had joined. Zaian casualty figures at El Herri (the French count of 182 is a French battlefield count). Whether the makhzen investiture made him an agent of the sultan or ratified power he already held.

name: Abdelkhalek Torres
aliasesRaw: عبد الخالق الطريس · Abdelkhalek Torres · Abd al-Khaliq al-Torres · Sp.: 'Abdeljalak Torres'
oneLine: Leader of nationalism in the Spanish zone; founder of the Partido de Reformas Nacionales at Tetouan.
contestedPoints: The extent of Spanish (and later Francoist) tolerance or sponsorship of northern nationalism as a lever against France, and how far that compromised the movement.

name: Moulay Hassan I
aliasesRaw: الحسن بن محمد (al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad) · Mawlay al-Hasan al-Awwal · Moulay Hassan I · Mulay Hasan · Muley Hassan (Sp.) · Mouley el-Hassan (Fr. consular usage) · Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad · 'the last great sultan' (historiographical epithet, not contemporary)
born: 1836 (conventional). Some reference works give 1857 — see Contradictions. Fez.
died: 9 June 1894, camp on the Oued el-Abid, Tadla region, returning from the Tafilalt harka. Buried Rabat.
oneLine: Alaouite sultan 1873–1894; attempted military and fiscal centralisation of the Makhzen under mounting European financial and territorial pressure.
contestedPoints: Birth year (1836 vs 1857). Exact year Mouha ou Hammou Zayani was made qaid (1877 / 1880 / 1886). Whether the 1893 Glaoui rescue and Krupp cannon story is documented or a literary elaboration by Gavin Maxwell. Whether his reforms failed on their own terms or were destroyed by the debt and protection regimes.

name: Emir Abd el-Malek
aliasesRaw: عبد الملك · Amir Abd el-Malek · Abd al-Malik al-Jaza'iri · Mulai Abdelmalek · Fr. archives: 'Abd el Malek' · Ottoman documents: Abdulmelik · Sp.: 'Abd-el-Malek'
died: not established — his movement is described as sustaining guerrilla war to 1919 and beyond
oneLine: Descendant of the Algerian emir Abd el-Kader and a former Ottoman officer; commanded the Ottoman- and German-backed resistance around Taza and the eastern Rif from 1915.
contestedPoints: Whether he was a son or a grandson of Abd el-Kader — two named scholars working from the same archives differ. His dates. Whether his movement was independent or 'forced to support the Germans for money and weapons'. His fate after 1918.

name: Ba Ahmed ibn Musa
aliasesRaw: أحمد بن موسى · Ahmad ibn Musa · Ba Ahmed · Ba Hmad · Fr.: 'le grand vizir Ba Ahmed'
oneLine: Chamberlain and grand vizier; concealed Hassan I's death in 1894 and ruled Morocco as regent for Abdelaziz until 1900.
contestedPoints: Whether his regency preserved the Makhzen or hollowed it out by excluding the sultan from government. His personal wealth and the Bahia palace.

name: Assou Oubasslam
aliasesRaw: عسو أوباسلام · Assou Ou Basslam · Assou u Baslam · Aassou Oubasslam · Fr.: 'Assou ou Ba Slam, chef des Aït Atta'

aliases.value: Assou ou Ba Slam, chef des Aït Atta
aliases.folded: assou ou ba slam, chef des ait atta

oneLine: Aït Atta commander at the siege of Bougafer (Jbel Saghro) in 1933, one of the last organised resistances to the French conquest.
contestedPoints: The terms on which Bougafer ended — negotiated terms or surrender. Casualties on both sides. Whether French aerial bombardment of civilians occurred, as Moroccan and Amazigh accounts hold.

name: Abderrahim Bouabid
aliasesRaw: عبد الرحيم بوعبيد · Abderrahim Bouabid
oneLine: Istiqlal then UNFP/USFP leader; economics minister at independence and the principal figure of the legal opposition until his death.
contestedPoints: The 1981 imprisonment over his position on the Western Sahara referendum — the limits of permitted dissent under Hassan II.

name: Hassan II
aliasesRaw: الحسن الثاني · Moulay Hassan ben Mohammed · Hassan II
oneLine: King 1961–1999; presided over the Years of Lead, two coup attempts, the Green March and the Western Sahara war.
contestedPoints: Command responsibility for the 1958–59 Rif repression, the 1965 Casablanca killings, Ben Barka, Tazmamart, and the disappearances. Almost every major question of this reign is contested and much of the record is closed.

name: Alphonse Juin
aliasesRaw: Alphonse Pierre Juin · Maréchal Juin
oneLine: Resident-General 1947–1951; confronted Mohammed V directly and began the campaign to isolate him from the Istiqlal.
contestedPoints: The extent to which he built the coalition of pashas and qaids later used to depose the sultan in 1953.

name: Mohamed Oufkir
aliasesRaw: محمد أوفقير · Mohamed Oufkir · General Oufkir
died: 16 August 1972, Rabat — official cause suicide; disputed
oneLine: French army officer who became interior minister and defence minister; central to the repression of the 1960s and to the Ben Barka affair; died after the 1972 coup attempt.
contestedPoints: The manner of his death (multiple gunshot wounds are reported, which is difficult to reconcile with suicide). His personal role in Ben Barka's death. The extent of his authorship of the 1972 coup attempt.

name: Charles Mangin
aliasesRaw: Charles Marie Emmanuel Mangin · Fr. press: 'le boucher' · 'the Butcher'
oneLine: Commanded the column that destroyed Ahmed al-Hiba at Sidi Bou Othmane, 6 September 1912; advocate of the 'Force Noire'.
contestedPoints: Casualty figures at Sidi Bou Othmane. His broader doctrine of using African colonial troops, and how it shaped who did the dying in Morocco.

name: Harry Maclean
aliasesRaw: Harry Aubrey de Vere Maclean · Caid Maclean · Kaid Sir Harry Maclean · Ar.: القائد ماكلين
oneLine: Scottish officer who commanded and trained the Moroccan sultan's army from the 1870s to 1907; kidnapped by Raisuni.
contestedPoints: Whether he served the sultan or British policy, and how far the two diverged. His influence over Abdelaziz. The terms of his ransom in 1907-08.

name: Samuel Gummere
aliasesRaw: Samuel Rene Gummere · Consul-General then Minister to Morocco
oneLine: American diplomat at Tangier during the Perdicaris affair of 1904 and the first US Minister to Morocco.
contestedPoints: How far the 'Perdicaris alive or Raisuli dead' telegram reflected policy as against domestic electioneering by Roosevelt.

name: Bou Hamara
aliasesRaw: بو حمارة ('the man on the she-donkey') · Jilali ben Driss al-Zarhuni al-Yusufi · Jilali Ben Driss Zerhouni · El Rogui / al-Rūgī ('the pretender') · Sp.: 'El Roghi', 'el Pretendiente' · Fr.: 'le Rogui Bou Hamara'

aliases.value: بو حمارة (the man on the she-donkey)
aliases.folded: بو حمارة (the man on the she-donkey)

died: September 1909 (2 September per one account), Fez
oneLine: Former Makhzen clerk who claimed to be the sultan's elder brother and ran a rival state in northeastern Morocco 1902–1909.
contestedPoints: Whether he genuinely claimed to be Moulay Mohammed or was so identified by his followers. The terms of the mining concessions he granted to Spanish and French interests. The manner of his execution — the 'fed to lions' story is repeated but poorly sourced.

name: Mohammed ben Abdelkrim El Khattabi
aliasesRaw: محمد بن عبد الكريم الخطابي · Abd el-Krim · Abd-el-Krim · Abdelkrim · Abd al-Karim al-Khattabi · Sp. archives: 'Abd-el-Krim', 'el cabecilla', 'el jefe rebelde' · Fr.: 'l'émir du Rif' · Tarifit: Muḥemmed n ʿEbdkrim Lxṭṭabi
oneLine: Qadi and Spanish-administration official who led the Rif war 1921–1926 and headed the Rif Republic; the most heavily documented Moroccan resistance figure in European archives.
contestedPoints: Whether the Rif Republic was a state, a proto-state or a confederation using modern vocabulary. Silvestre's death (suicide vs killed vs unknown). Annual casualty figures (7,875 to 13,363 depending on source and definition). Whether the 1925 attack on the French zone was overreach or a forced choice. His dealings with foreign mining interests.

name: Taher Bey
aliasesRaw: Tahir Bey · Taher Bey · Yanyalı Tahir Bey · the name appears as both Tahir and Taher in the two principal studies

aliases.value: the name appears as both Tahir and Taher in the two principal studies
aliases.folded: the name appears as both tahir and taher in the two principal studies

oneLine: Ottoman major who headed the Teşkilât-ı Mahsusa mission to Morocco from Madrid, 1914–1916.
contestedPoints: Why he was dismissed in early 1916 — the sources say German pressure. Whether his assessments of tribal leaders were accurate or self-serving.

name: M'Hammad ben Abdelkrim El Khattabi
aliasesRaw: محمد بن عبد الكريم · M'Hamed / Mhamed / M'Hammad Abd el-Krim · Sp.: 'el hermano de Abd-el-Krim'
oneLine: Brother of Abd el-Krim; mining engineer trained in Spain, field commander and the Rif Republic's technical and diplomatic organiser.
contestedPoints: Division of authority between the brothers. His role in the Republic's foreign contacts and in the mining question.

name: Moulay Youssef
aliasesRaw: يوسف بن الحسن · Yusef of Morocco · Moulay Youssef ben Hassan
oneLine: Sultan 1912–1927; installed by Lyautey after Abdelhafid's abdication and reigned throughout the pacification wars.
contestedPoints: Whether he exercised any independent authority. His role, if any, in the Rif war and in the wartime German approaches.

name: Ahmed Balafrej
aliasesRaw: أحمد بلفريج · Ahmed Balafrej · Fr.: 'Balafrej'
oneLine: Istiqlal secretary-general and drafter of the 1944 Independence Manifesto; first foreign minister of independent Morocco.
contestedPoints: His authorship share of the 1944 Manifesto. His role in the internationalisation strategy at the UN and in the Arab League.

name: Hugo Stoltzenberg
aliasesRaw: Hugo Stoltzenberg · Chemische Fabrik Stoltzenberg, Hamburg
oneLine: German chemist who supplied Spain with chemical weapons capability for the Rif war, in breach of the Versailles Treaty.
contestedPoints: Quantities supplied and delivery dates. The German government's knowledge and involvement. His role in building La Marañosa.

name: Dámaso Berenguer
aliasesRaw: Dámaso Berenguer y Fusté, conde de Xauen · 'el Alto Comisario'

aliases.value: Dámaso Berenguer y Fusté, conde de Xauen
aliases.folded: damaso berenguer y fuste, conde de xauen

oneLine: High Commissioner in Morocco 1919–1922; found negligent by the Expediente Picasso and the author of the documented authorisation of chemical munitions.
contestedPoints: His degree of responsibility for Silvestre's advance. Whether the amnesty was political protection. The chain of command for chemical weapons after August 1921.

name: Philippe Pétain
aliasesRaw: Henri Philippe Bénoni Omer Joseph Pétain · Maréchal Pétain

aliases.value: Henri Philippe Bénoni Omer Joseph Pétain
aliases.folded: henri philippe benoni omer joseph petain

oneLine: Sent to Morocco in 1925 with authority over Lyautey to defeat Abd el-Krim; later head of the Vichy state.
contestedPoints: The extent of French participation in, or knowledge of, chemical weapons use in the Rif. Whether his appointment was intended to displace Lyautey.

name: Abdelhadi Boutaleb
aliasesRaw: عبد الهادي بوطالب · Abdelhadi Boutaleb
oneLine: Tutor to Hassan II, minister, ambassador and secretary-general of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference; a memoirist of the palace.
contestedPoints: The reliability of his memoirs, which are among the few insider accounts of the palace and are written by a loyal servant of it.

name: Paul Prosper Henrys
aliasesRaw: Paul Prosper Henrys · Général Henrys
oneLine: Commanded French forces in the Middle Atlas from 1914; took Taza and Khénifra and directed the Zaian war after El Herri.
contestedPoints: His prior knowledge of Laverdure's intentions before 13 November 1914. The human cost of the 'submit or starve' policy he adopted afterwards.

name: Mohamed Hassan Ouazzani
aliasesRaw: محمد بن الحسن الوزاني · Ouazzani · Wazzani · Fr.: 'El Ouezzani'
oneLine: Nationalist leader and journalist; split from Allal El Fassi in 1937 to found a rival party, and remained outside Istiqlal thereafter.
contestedPoints: The causes of the 1937 split — personal, ideological, or over the movement's relationship to the throne.

name: Abdallah Ibrahim
aliasesRaw: عبد الله إبراهيم · Abdallah Ibrahim · Abdellah Ibrahim
oneLine: Prime minister 1958–1960; led the only government of independent Morocco to attempt a socialist economic programme.
contestedPoints: Why his government was dismissed in May 1960 and how far its economic programme had actually gone.

name: Joseph-François Poeymirau
aliasesRaw: Joseph-François Poeymirau · Général Poeymirau · Fr.: 'Poeymirau le fougueux'
oneLine: Succeeded Henrys in the Middle Atlas; established French control of the Moulouya and received the submission of Mouha ou Hammou's sons in 1920.
contestedPoints: The terms offered to the Zaian sons in June 1920 — what was promised, and whether it was kept.

name: M'barek Bekkay
aliasesRaw: المبارك البكاي · M'Barek Bekkai Lahbil · Si Bekkay · Fr.: 'le colonel Bekkay'
oneLine: French army officer who resigned as pasha of Sefrou over the 1953 deposition and became independent Morocco's first prime minister.
contestedPoints: Whether his appointment in 1955 was a nationalist choice or a compromise designed to reassure France.

name: Henri Gouraud
aliasesRaw: Henri Joseph Eugène Gouraud · Général Gouraud · 'le manchot' (after losing an arm at Gallipoli)

aliases.value: le manchot (after losing an arm at Gallipoli)
aliases.folded: le manchot (after losing an arm at gallipoli)

oneLine: Commanded in Mauritania against Ma al-'Aynayn's networks and in Morocco from 1911; later High Commissioner in the Levant.
contestedPoints: His conduct of the Mauritanian campaigns and the destruction of Saharan religious centres.

name: Mehdi Ben Barka
aliasesRaw: المهدي بن بركة · Mehdi Ben Barka · El Mehdi Ben Barka
died: Disappeared 29 October 1965, Paris. Body never found; date and manner of death not established.
oneLine: Mathematician, Istiqlal then UNFP leader and Tricontinental organiser; abducted in Paris in 1965 and never seen again.
contestedPoints: Who ordered it; whether Hassan II authorised it directly; the roles of Oufkir, Dlimi, French police and services, Mossad and the CIA; where the body is. French files remain classified; c. 1,800 CIA documents acknowledged and undisclosed.

name: Augustin Guillaume
aliasesRaw: Augustin Léon Guillaume · Général Guillaume
oneLine: Resident-General 1951–1954; executed the deposition and exile of Mohammed V in August 1953.
contestedPoints: Whether he initiated the deposition, executed a decision taken in Paris, or was carried along by El Glaoui and the notables. All three versions are in circulation.

name: Shakib Arslan
aliasesRaw: شكيب أرسلان · Shakib Arslan · 'amīr al-bayān' · Fr.: 'l'émir Chekib Arslan'
oneLine: Druze-Lebanese pan-Islamic publicist based in Geneva who internationalised the Moroccan campaign against the 1930 Berber dahir.
contestedPoints: The extent of his direct influence on the Moroccan nationalist leadership as against parallel development. His wartime political alignments.

name: Juan Picasso González
aliasesRaw: Juan Picasso González · 'el general Picasso' · the Expediente Picasso
oneLine: Spanish general appointed to investigate the Annual disaster; author of the inquiry that remains the primary documentary base for it.
contestedPoints: How much of the original file survives and in what condition. What his brief permitted him to investigate and what it excluded.

name: Thami El Glaoui
aliasesRaw: التهامي الڣلاوي · Thami el Glaoui · T'hami El Glaoui · Si Thami · 'le Glaoui' · 'the Lord of the Atlas' (English literary coinage, Gavin Maxwell) · 'le Pacha de Marrakech' · Sp.: 'el Glaui'

aliases.value: the Lord of the Atlas (English literary coinage
aliases.folded: the lord of the atlas (english literary coinage

oneLine: Pasha of Marrakech 1907–1956 and the Protectorate's principal Moroccan intermediary in the south; central actor in the 1953 deposition of Mohammed V.
contestedPoints: Whether the 1893 Telouet rescue and Krupp cannon story is documented or literary. The size of his fortune (the $50m figure is an estimate of unclear origin). Whether the 1953 deposition was his initiative or a French operation using him. Whether his 1955 submission was conviction, calculation, or coercion by his own family.

name: Ali Amhaouch
aliasesRaw: علي أمهاوش · Sidi Ali Amhaouch · Ali Amhawch · Fr.: 'le marabout Amhaouch', 'le chef religieux des Aït Sokhman'

aliases.value: le chef religieux des Aït Sokhman
aliases.folded: le chef religieux des ait sokhman

died: 1918, before the end of the Zaian war; natural causes per the standard account
oneLine: Darqawi-linked religious leader of the Middle Atlas whose spiritual authority organised resistance across tribal boundaries.
contestedPoints: Extent of his authority. His relationship with Mouha ou Hammou — alliance, rivalry, or division of spheres. His prophecies, which French intelligence took seriously as a mobilising force.

name: Ahmed Bahnini
aliasesRaw: أحمد باحنيني · Ahmed Bahnini
oneLine: Jurist and prime minister 1963–1965; killed in the Skhirat palace attack of 10 July 1971.
contestedPoints: His government's handling of the 1963 opposition trials and the 1965 crisis.

name: Mohammed IV
aliasesRaw: محمد بن عبد الرحمن · Sidi Mohammed ben Abderrahmane · Muley Mohamed (Sp.)
oneLine: Sultan 1859–1873; lost the Hispano-Moroccan war of 1859–60 and accepted the indemnity that mortgaged Moroccan customs.
contestedPoints: Size and payment mechanism of the Tetouan indemnity, and what share of state revenue it consumed.

name: Moulay Abdelhafid
aliasesRaw: عبد الحفيظ بن الحسن (ʿAbd al-Ḥafīẓ ibn al-Ḥasan) · Abd al-Hafid · Moulay Hafid (Fr. usage) · Muley Hafid (Sp.) · Mulai Hafid (Ger./Br. press) · al-Sulṭān al-Ḥāfiẓ

aliases.value: عبد الحفيظ بن الحسن (ʿAbd al-Ḥafīẓ ibn al-Ḥasan)
aliases.folded: عبد الحفيظ بن الحسن (abd al-hafiz ibn al-hasan)

born: 24 February 1875 or 1876, Fez — not securely established
died: 4 April 1937, Enghien-les-Bains, France. Buried Fez, Moulay Abdallah necropolis.
oneLine: Alaouite sultan 1908–1912; came to power on an explicitly anti-European conditional bay'a and signed the Treaty of Fez four years later.
contestedPoints: The exact text and binding force of the 1908 conditional bay'a. Whether he signed the Treaty of Fez under duress or negotiated terms. The 'fed Bou Hamara to his lions' story — widely repeated, poorly sourced. Whether his 1911 appeal for French help was voluntary or manufactured. The discrepancy between the Arabic and French texts of the 1912 treaty.

name: Moulay Abdelaziz
aliasesRaw: عبد العزيز بن الحسن (ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn al-Ḥasan) · Abd al-Aziz · Abdelaziz IV · Moulay Abd el-Aziz (Fr.) · Muley Abd-el-Aziz (Sp.) · Abdul Aziz (Br. press) · 'le sultan aux jouets' (hostile French press epithet)

aliases.value: عبد العزيز بن الحسن (ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn al-Ḥasan)
aliases.folded: عبد العزيز بن الحسن (abd al-aziz ibn al-hasan)

aliases.value: le sultan aux jouets (hostile French press epithet)
aliases.folded: le sultan aux jouets (hostile french press epithet)

died: 1943, Tangier. Buried Fez, Moulay Abdallah necropolis.
oneLine: Alaouite sultan 1894–1908; his reign covers the fiscal capture of the Makhzen by European lenders and the diplomatic partition of Morocco between 1904 and 1906.
contestedPoints: Birth year. Whether the tertib failed because of its design, its collectors, or a deliberate campaign against it. Whether he was personally frivolous (the European press caricature, later recycled by nationalist historiography) or structurally trapped. Casualty figures for the Casablanca bombardment. Whether Ba Ahmed's regency stabilised or hollowed out the Makhzen.

name: Si Madani El Glaoui
aliasesRaw: المدني الڣلاوي · Si Madani el Glaoui · El Madani · Fr.: 'le grand vizir El Madani'
oneLine: Elder brother of Thami; head of the Glaoua, grand vizier under Abdelhafid, and the actual architect of the family's rise.
contestedPoints: How the power was divided between the brothers before 1918. His role in engineering the Hafidiya.

name: Mohammed ben Arafa
aliasesRaw: محمد بن عرفة · Mohammed Ben Aarafa · Moulay Ben Arafa · Fr.: 'le sultan Ben Arafa'
oneLine: Installed as sultan by the French and El Glaoui in August 1953 after the deposition of Mohammed V; never accepted; removed 1955.
contestedPoints: Whether he sought the throne or was compelled. The bay'a he received — who signed it and under what pressure. The two assassination attempts against him.

name: Francisco Franco
aliasesRaw: Francisco Franco Bahamonde · 'el Caudillo' · Fr.: 'Franco'
oneLine: Made his career in the Rif war; commanded the Legion at Alhucemas; launched the 1936 coup from Morocco with Moroccan troops.
contestedPoints: His personal involvement in chemical weapons operations. Recruitment methods for the Regulares in 1936. Whether Spanish tolerance of Moroccan nationalism after 1936 was policy or expedient.

name: Sidi Mohamed Ben Hammou — identification unresolved
aliasesRaw: Name as supplied. Candidate identifications and their variants are set out in the page body. Do not merge with Mouha ou Hammou Zayani or with his sons without evidence.

aliases.value: Name as supplied. Candidate identifications and their variants are set out in the page body. Do not merge with Mouha ou Hammou Zayani or with his sons without evidence.
aliases.folded: name as supplied. candidate identifications and their variants are set out in the page body. do not merge with mouha ou hammou zayani or with his sons without evidence.

oneLine: A name requiring identification before any biography can be written.
contestedPoints: Everything. The name as given matches several distinct people and no identification has been established.

name: Salah Sharif at-Tunisi
aliasesRaw: صالح الشريف التونسي · Salah Sharif at-Tunisi · Salih al-Sharif al-Tunisi
oneLine: Tunisian scholar who wrote the pan-Islamic propaganda distributed in Morocco during the First World War.
contestedPoints: The reach and effect of the pamphlets. Whether the Tamazight-language material was actually produced or only planned.

name: Eugène Regnault
aliasesRaw: Eugène Regnault · 'le ministre Regnault'
oneLine: French minister at Tangier who negotiated and signed the Treaty of Fez with Moulay Abdelhafid on 30 March 1912.
contestedPoints: What pressure was applied during the negotiation of 29-30 March 1912. Whether he was aware of, or responsible for, any divergence between the Arabic and French texts.

name: Miguel Primo de Rivera
aliasesRaw: Miguel Primo de Rivera y Orbaneja, marqués de Estella · 'el Dictador'

aliases.value: Miguel Primo de Rivera y Orbaneja, marqués de Estella
aliases.folded: miguel primo de rivera y orbaneja, marques de estella

oneLine: Dictator of Spain 1923–1930; came to power on the Annual crisis and directed the war that destroyed the Rif Republic.
contestedPoints: Whether he was an abandonista who reversed himself or a pragmatist who waited for French co-belligerence. His authorisation of chemical weapons use.

name: Joseph Gallieni
aliasesRaw: Joseph-Simon Gallieni · Maréchal Gallieni (posthumous, 1921)
oneLine: Colonial commander in Sudan, Tonkin and Madagascar; Lyautey's mentor and the originator of the doctrine applied in Morocco.
contestedPoints: How much of the 'tache d'huile' method was his and how much Lyautey's later systematisation and self-promotion.

name: Moulay Abderrahmane
aliasesRaw: عبد الرحمن بن هشام · Abd al-Rahman ibn Hisham · Muley Abderrahman (Sp.)
oneLine: Sultan 1822–1859; support for Abd al-Qadir led to defeat at Isly (1844) and the first treaty concessions to France.
contestedPoints: Scale of the Isly defeat. Whether support for Abd al-Qadir was strategic or forced by popular pressure.

name: Alfonso XIII
aliasesRaw: Alfonso XIII de Borbón · 'el Rey Alfonso'
oneLine: King of Spain 1886–1931; his reign covers the whole Spanish protectorate project and the Annual disaster that helped end it.
contestedPoints: Whether he encouraged Silvestre's 1921 advance by direct telegram over the heads of government and High Commissioner. Alleged, never proven. His role in shelving the Expediente Picasso and in amnestying Berenguer.

name: Ma al-'Aynayn
aliasesRaw: ماء العينين · Ma al-ʿAynayn · Ma el Ainïn · Ma El Aininn · Cheikh Ma el Ainín (Fr.) · Ma-el-Ainin (Sp.) · birth name Muḥammad Muṣṭafā wuld Muḥammad Faḍil · Fr. archives: 'le marabout Ma el Aïnin', 'le cheikh du Sahara'

aliases.value: birth name Muḥammad Muṣṭafā wuld Muḥammad Faḍil
aliases.folded: birth name muhammad mustafa wuld muhammad fadil

oneLine: Sufi shaykh, scholar and Makhzen khalifa of the Sahara; founder of Smara and organiser of Saharan resistance to French expansion.
contestedPoints: Whether he acted as a Makhzen agent or an autonomous sovereign, and when that changed. Whether he formally claimed the sultanate in 1910. The Spanish role in arming him — asserted in French reporting, an interested claim. His date of birth. The real strength of his following.

name: Ahmed Dlimi
aliasesRaw: أحمد الدليمي · Ahmed Dlimi · General Dlimi
died: 25 January 1983, near Marrakech — officially a road accident; widely disputed
oneLine: Security chief and later commander of Moroccan forces in the Western Sahara; implicated in the Ben Barka affair; died in disputed circumstances in 1983.
contestedPoints: His role in the Ben Barka abduction — he surrendered voluntarily to the French court and was acquitted. The circumstances of his death, which almost no independent account accepts as accidental.

name: Driss Basri
aliasesRaw: إدريس البصري · Driss Basri
oneLine: Interior minister 1979–1999; the operational architect of Hassan II's internal control system and of the Western Sahara administration.
contestedPoints: The extent of his personal responsibility versus the king's for the Years of Lead. Election management. His dismissal in November 1999 and what it signalled.

name: Mohammed V
aliasesRaw: محمد الخامس · Sidi Mohammed ben Youssef · Mohammed ben Youssef · Fr.: 'Sidi Mohammed', 'le Sultan' · Sp.: 'Mohamed V' · Sultan 1927–1957, King from 1957
oneLine: Sultan from 1927 and King from 1957; installed by France as a compliant minor and became the central symbol of Moroccan independence.
contestedPoints: Whether he signed the 1930 Berber dahir freely, under duress, or without grasping its consequences. The extent and nature of his protection of Moroccan Jews under Vichy. What Roosevelt actually said at Anfa in 1943. Whether the 1953 deposition was primarily French or Glaoui-driven. His responsibility for the 1958-59 Rif repression.

name: Moha ou Said
aliasesRaw: محا أو سعيد · Moha ou Saïd · Mouha ou Said · Moha u Saʿid · Fr.: 'Moha ou Saïd, chef des Aït Ouirra'

aliases.value: Moha ou Saïd, chef des Aït Ouirra
aliases.folded: moha ou said, chef des ait ouirra

oneLine: Aït Ouirra leader who fought France from before 1912 until his death in 1924, outlasting the Zaian war by three years.
contestedPoints: His birth date and early career. His relationship with Mouha ou Hammou — the two are frequently confused in the literature, including by name.

name: Ahmed al-Hiba
aliasesRaw: أحمد الهيبة · El Hiba · Ahmed el-Hiba · al-Sulṭān al-Azraq / 'le Sultan Bleu' / 'el Sultán Azul' · Fr.: 'le prétendant El Hiba'

aliases.value: al-Sulṭān al-Azraq / le Sultan Bleu / el Sultán Azul
aliases.folded: al-sultan al-azraq / le sultan bleu / el sultan azul

oneLine: Son of Ma al-'Aynayn; proclaimed sultan at Tiznit in 1912, took Marrakech, and was destroyed at Sidi Bou Othmane on 6 September 1912.
contestedPoints: Exact death date. Scale of his following. Whether the sultanate claim was widely accepted or confined to the south. The fate of the French hostages taken at Marrakech.

name: Mohamed Ameziane
aliasesRaw: محمد أمزيان · Sharif Mohamed Ameziane · Mohand Ameziane · Sp.: 'El Mizzian', 'el Cherif Mohamed Amezian'
oneLine: Rifian leader of resistance to Spanish expansion around Melilla 1909–1912; commanded at the Barranco del Lobo.
contestedPoints: Spanish casualty figures at the Barranco del Lobo (July 1909). Whether he acted with Makhzen sanction. Circumstances of his death.

name: José Sanjurjo
aliasesRaw: José Sanjurjo Sacanell, marqués del Rif · 'el León del Rif'

aliases.value: José Sanjurjo Sacanell, marqués del Rif
aliases.folded: jose sanjurjo sacanell, marques del rif

oneLine: Africanista commander in the Rif war, ennobled as marqués del Rif; nominal leader of the July 1936 coup, killed in an air crash days into it.
contestedPoints: His role in the Alhucemas landing relative to other commanders. The extent of his authority over the 1936 rising.

name: Manuel Fernández Silvestre
aliasesRaw: Manuel Fernández Silvestre y Pantiga · 'el general Silvestre'
died: 22 July 1921, Annual — manner of death not established
oneLine: Comandante General of Melilla; drove the advance that collapsed at Annual in July 1921 and died there.
contestedPoints: Suicide, killed in action, or unknown — no version is documented. Whether he acted on royal encouragement. Whether his conduct was recklessness or the execution of an agreed policy.

name: Hubert Lyautey
aliasesRaw: Louis-Hubert Gonzalve Lyautey · Maréchal Lyautey · 'le Résident' · Ar. usage: ليوطي · in Moroccan sources often simply 'al-Ḥāmī al-ʿĀmm' (the Resident-General)

aliases.value: in Moroccan sources often simply al-Ḥāmī al-ʿĀmm (the Resident-General)
aliases.folded: in moroccan sources often simply al-hami al-amm (the resident-general)

died: 27 July 1934, Thorey-Lyautey. Interred in Rabat; remains repatriated to Les Invalides, Paris, 1961.
oneLine: First French Resident-General of Morocco 1912–1925; architect of the Protectorate's system of indirect rule, urban segregation and 'pacification'.
contestedPoints: Whether 'respect for Moroccan institutions' was principle or technique. Whether he authored or merely inherited the Berber policy. His degree of responsibility for El Herri. Whether the villes nouvelles preserved the medinas or ghettoised them. The circumstances of his 1925 resignation.

name: René Laverdure
aliasesRaw: René Laverdure · Lieutenant-colonel Laverdure
oneLine: Commander at Khénifra; marched without orders on 13 November 1914 and was killed with 623 of his men at El Herri.
contestedPoints: His motive. Whether he acted on intelligence that Mouha ou Hammou was personally in the camp. How much his superiors knew in advance.

name: Maurice Le Glay
aliasesRaw: Maurice Le Glay · 'le contrôleur civil Le Glay'
oneLine: Officer of Affaires Indigènes, Berberist ethnographer and writer; named in the literature as an author of the policy behind the 1930 dahir.
contestedPoints: His actual authorship of the 1930 dahir versus his role as its intellectual precursor. Whether his ethnography is usable evidence or ideology.

name: Mohamed Lyazidi
aliasesRaw: محمد اليزيدي · Mohamed Lyazidi · al-Yazidi
oneLine: Nationalist organiser from the 1930 anti-dahir campaign onward; signatory of the 1944 Independence Manifesto.
contestedPoints: His organisational role relative to the better-known leaders — probably underestimated.

name: Allal El Fassi
aliasesRaw: علال الفاسي · Allal al-Fassi · Fr.: 'Allal el Fassi'
oneLine: Salafi scholar and founder-leader of the Istiqlal party; the dominant intellectual figure of Moroccan nationalism.
contestedPoints: His 'Greater Morocco' territorial doctrine and its later use in the Western Sahara conflict. His relationship with the monarchy after 1956. The degree of Salafi versus liberal content in his programme.

name: Abderrahmane Youssoufi
aliasesRaw: عبد الرحمن اليوسفي · Abderrahmane Youssoufi
oneLine: Resistance lawyer, UNFP/USFP leader, death-sentenced in absentia and long exiled; prime minister of the 1998 alternance government.
contestedPoints: Whether the 1998 alternance was a genuine democratic transition or a managed co-optation of the opposition. His own later published reservations bear on this.

name: Ahmed al-Raisuni
aliasesRaw: أحمد الريسوني · Raisuni · Raisuli · Er Raisuli · Mulai Ahmed er Raisuni · Sp.: 'el Raisuni' · Br. press: 'the Raisuli'
oneLine: Sharifian notable of the Jebala; kidnapper, pasha of Tangier and Asilah, and by turns opponent and instrument of Spain.
contestedPoints: Whether he was a bandit, a politician using kidnapping as leverage, or a Spanish client — arguably all three at different dates. The Perdicaris ransom terms. Circumstances of his capture and death in 1925.

name: Germain Ayache
aliasesRaw: Germain Ayache · جرمان عياش
oneLine: Moroccan historian who founded a national school of Moroccan history written against colonial historiography; author of Les origines de la guerre du Rif.
contestedPoints: His dates as recorded here are the conventional ones and have not been verified in this session. How far his method genuinely escaped the colonial framework he attacked.

name: Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Nasiri
aliasesRaw: أحمد بن خالد الناصري · al-Nasiri al-Slawi · an-Nasiri · Fr.: 'Ahmed Ben Khaled en-Naciri es-Slaoui' · Ennaciri · An-Nasiri
oneLine: Moroccan historian; author of Kitab al-Istiqsa, the first comprehensive national history of Morocco, completed in 1894.
contestedPoints: His exact birth date (March vs April 1835). How far his account of European encroachment is shaped by his position inside the Makhzen order. Whether his use of European sources makes him more reliable or differently compromised.

name: Zaïd Ou Hmad
aliasesRaw: زايد أو حماد · Zayd u Hmad · Zaïd Ou Hmad · Zaïd Ouhmad. Spelling not standardised; French archival forms not yet established.

aliases.value: Zaïd Ouhmad. Spelling not standardised; French archival forms not yet established.
aliases.folded: zaid ouhmad. spelling not standardised; french archival forms not yet established.

oneLine: Resistance leader active 1934-1936, after the date France declared the pacification of Morocco complete.
contestedPoints: Everything — dates, region, tribe, the scale of his following. Identified in Session 4 from a Moroccan state publication and not yet researched anywhere else.

name: Mohammed Sellam Ameziane
aliasesRaw: محمد سلام أمزيان · Sellam Amezian · Salam Amezyan · Mohammed Sellam Ameziane. Not to be confused with Mohamed Ameziane (d. 1912), the Rif leader against Spain — different men, similar names, half a century apart.

aliases.value: Mohammed Sellam Ameziane. Not to be confused with Mohamed Ameziane (d. 1912), the Rif leader against Spain — different men, similar names, half a century apart.
aliases.folded: mohammed sellam ameziane. not to be confused with mohamed ameziane (d. 1912), the rif leader against spain — different men, similar names, half a century apart.

died: not established — escaped to Spain, then Egypt and Iraq
oneLine: Qarawiyyin graduate and Liberation Army veteran who directed the 1958-59 Rif revolt against the independent Moroccan government.
contestedPoints: His dates and fate. Whether the 18-point programme was his drafting. Whether the revolt sought reform within the state or something more.

name: Abdallah Laroui
aliasesRaw: عبد الله العروي · Abdallah Laroui · Abdellah Laroui · al-ʿArwi
died: living as of the sources consulted
oneLine: Moroccan historian and philosopher; the most influential critic of colonial and orientalist historiography of Morocco.
contestedPoints: Whether his Marxist framework substitutes one external theory for another. His later testimony on Hassan II, written by a man who had access to the palace.
